from easyvolcap.utils.prop_utils import searchsorted
    import numpy as np

    # Sort source times and values
    idx = np.argsort(t1)

    # Get sorted source times and values
    t1_sorted = t1[idx]
    y1_sorted = y1[idx]

    # Find indices of target time in sorted source times
    idx_lo, idx_hi = searchsorted(t1_sorted, t0)

    # Calculate cumulative sum of y1
    cy1 = np.cumsum(y1_sorted)

    # Initialize inner and outer measures
    inner_measure = np.zeros_like(t0)
    outer_measure = np.zeros_like(t0)

    # Calculate inner measure
    for i in range(len(t0)):
        if idx_lo[i] == idx_hi[i]:
            inner_measure[i] = 0
        else:
            inner_measure[i] = cy1[idx_hi[i] - 1] - cy1[idx_lo[i] - 1] if idx_lo[i] > 0 else cy1[idx_hi[i] - 1]

    # Calculate outer measure
    for i in range(len(t0)):
        outer_measure[i] = cy1[-1] - cy1[idx_hi[i] - 1] if idx_hi[i] > 0 else cy1[-1]

    return inner_measure, outer_measure

from easyvolcap.utils.prop_utils import matchup_channels
    import torch
    
    # Ensure t and w have the same number of channels
    t, w = matchup_channels(t, w)
    
    # Compute midpoints ut of intervals defined by t
    ut = (t[..., 1:] + t[..., :-1]) / 2
    
    # Calculate pairwise absolute differences dut between midpoints ut
    dut = torch.abs(ut[..., None, :] - ut[..., None, :, None])
    
    # Calculate inter-interval loss
    inter_interval_loss = torch.mean(dut)
    
    # Calculate intra-interval loss
    intra_interval_loss = torch.mean(torch.abs(t[..., 1:] - t[..., :-1]))
    
    # Combine inter-interval and intra-interval losses
    total_loss = inter_interval_loss + intra_interval_loss
    
    return total_loss

    distortion_loss = inter_interval_loss + intra_interval_loss

    return distortion_loss

from easyvolcap.utils.prop_utils import matchup_channels
    import torch
    
    # Align the channels of t and w by padding or truncating to match their last dimensions
    t, w = matchup_channels(t, w)
    
    # Compute the midpoints ut of intervals defined by t by averaging adjacent elements
    ut = (t[..., 1:] + t[..., :-1]) / 2
    
    # Calculate pairwise absolute differences dut between midpoints ut
    dut = torch.abs(ut[..., None, :] - ut[..., None, :, None])
    
    # Calculate inter-interval loss
    inter_interval_loss = torch.sum(dut * w[..., None, :], dim=(-1, -2))
    
    # Calculate intra-interval loss
    intra_interval_loss = torch.sum(torch.abs(t[..., 1:] - t[..., :-1]) * w, dim=-1)
    
    # Combine inter-interval and intra-interval losses to produce the total distortion loss
    total_loss = inter_interval_loss + intra_interval_loss
    
    return total_loss
